note: MAN-40 pins the digest to RFC 8785 (JCS) over the document with digest and
signature removed. Two implementations must therefore produce the same
string, and a probe that canonicalises differently reports a failure on a
correct publisher. These cases exist so the probe (machine/conformance.py)
and the Go implementation (vireo ComputeDigest) are checked against the same
bytes rather than against each other's assumptions.
Each case is a document and the digest both implementations must compute.
The cases deliberately include non-ASCII text: Python's json.dumps escapes
it as \uXXXX by default while Go emits UTF-8, and that disagreement is the
defect this fixture exists to catch.

cases.name: non-ascii-description
cases.note: A business with an accented and non-Latin name. Python must not escape it.

agents.name: support
agents.description: Bonjour, こんにちは — naïve questions welcome

cases.name: markup-in-description
cases.note: MAN-11 says descriptions are plain text; if one carries < & > anyway, Go must not escape them and Python must not either.

cases.name: unsorted-members
cases.note: Member order in the source must not matter: both canonicalisers sort.
